_what: Sourced laminate material minima. DATA ONLY — no arithmetic lives here.
_rule: Every row carries source + kind. kind=published means a page was fetched and quoted. A row whose source is null is NOT usable: s_stackup_budget.py refuses to compute with it and exits 2 (CANNOT DETERMINE). That refusal is the point — a missing number must stay missing.
_convention: FRONT = the component side (Apple's FCC filing). See docs/REFERENCE-TEARDOWN.md header.

1oz.source: PCBWay capabilities page, 'Outer layers: 1oz through 8oz (35um-280um)' — fetched 2026-09-05 https://www.pcbway.com/capabilities.html

0.5oz.source: JLCPCB PCB capabilities, 'Inner Layer: 0.5 oz / 1 oz / 2 oz'; 0.5 oz = half of the 1 oz = 35 um published above — fetched 2026-09-05 https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities

0.33oz.source: IPC-4562 nominal 12 um foil (1/3 oz). NOT fetched from a fabricator page in this session.

outer_finished_copper._why: An outer layer is base foil PLUS electroplated copper in and around the holes. The finished outer copper is what occupies the thickness budget, not the foil alone.

economy.source: PCBWay/JLCPCB both publish 1 oz as the standard FINISHED outer weight for multilayer.

thin.source: 0.33 oz foil + ~13 um plate. Arithmetic on the foil row above; no fabricator page fetched stating a 25 um finished outer.

hdi_min.source: PCBWay HDI capability page: "Finished copper: 18um-70um" — https://www.pcbway.com/hdi-pcb.html , fetched 2026-09-05. The thin end taken.

core._why: A core is laminate with copper already on both faces; it sets the floor for how thin an inner-layer pair can be.

fr4_min_rigid.source: Two independent pages agree that 0.1 mm is the thin end of stocked rigid FR-4 core, and that 0.05-0.08 mm 'typically require flexible polyimide substrates' — allpcb.com/allelectrohub/the-definitive-guide-to-pcb-core-thickness-choosing-whats-right-for-your-design and pcbsync.com/0-1mm-pcb/, fetched 2026-09-05

ultrathin_hdi._note: Apple's suppliers build any-layer HDI with cores well under 0.10 mm. No published capability page giving a number was fetched in this session, so this row is deliberately null and the hdi-ultrathin construction below cannot be evaluated. Filling this in from memory would be the exact defect this project keeps producing.

hdi_laser_blind_min.source: PCBWay HDI capability page, verbatim: "In standard prototyping, the minimum core thickness for laser blind vias is 0.1mm." — https://www.pcbway.com/hdi-pcb.html , fetched 2026-09-05
hdi_laser_blind_min._read_precisely: This is the minimum core that will be LASER-DRILLED for blind vias, not necessarily the thinnest core the house stocks. It is the number that binds an HDI build, which is what this row is for.

prepreg._why: Prepreg is the glass-and-resin sheet that bonds the stack; its PRESSED thickness is what counts, and that is style-dependent.

106.source: MADPCB 'PP 106: thickness 50um' and Bittele/advancedpcb charts, ~2 mil = 0.05 mm — https://madpcb.com/pp/ , fetched 2026-09-05

1080.source: MADPCB 'PP 1080: 60-70 um'; ~2.5 mil = 0.064 mm elsewhere. Midpoint 0.065 used. — https://madpcb.com/pp/ , fetched 2026-09-05

2116.source: MADPCB 'PP 2116: 90-110 um'; ~4.5 mil = 0.114 mm elsewhere. Midpoint 0.100 used. — https://madpcb.com/pp/ , fetched 2026-09-05

hdi_laser_blind_min.source: PCBWay HDI capability page, verbatim: "In standard prototyping, the minimum PP thickness for laser blind vias is 0.06mm." — https://www.pcbway.com/hdi-pcb.html , fetched 2026-09-05
hdi_laser_blind_min._note: THICKER than the 0.050 mm type-106 prepreg used in fr4-thin. HDI does not mean thinner dielectric at this house.

soldermask_per_side.source: No fabricator page giving a soldermask film thickness was fetched. This is the customary 10-20 um over laminate and is carried as a RANGE and as an INFERENCE, never folded into a single stack number.

fr4-economy._desc: what a prototype house stocks and quotes without a review

fr4-thin._desc: thinnest rigid FR-4 build using stocked material at its published thin end

hdi-ultrathin._desc: any-layer HDI of the class Apple's suppliers run, with cores below any published prototype capability. STILL UNEVALUABLE BY DESIGN — no page giving such a number has been fetched. Distinct from hdi-pcbway-published, which is a real house's real published HDI floor.

hdi-pcbway-published._desc: HDI built to the thinnest numbers PCBWay publishes for laser blind vias. Added 2026-09-05 to fill what was a deliberately null row.

fabricator_capability._what: What a real fabricator will BUILD, read off published capability pages only. No account was created, no quote requested, nobody contacted.

pcbway.moq: CANNOT DETERMINE — the capabilities page publishes no prototype MOQ, and finding one would need the ordering flow. Not pursued: no accounts, no quotes.

jlcpcb.min_thickness_overall_note: 0.4 mm, and the page gives it for 2-layer only
jlcpcb.thickness_options_4_layer_mm_CAVEAT: the fetch returned 0.8/1.0/1.2/1.6/2.0 for 4-layer but flagged it as INFERRED from the standard offering rather than quoted. Treat the 4-layer row as UNVERIFIED; the overall 0.4 mm minimum is the quoted figure.

fabricator_capability._the_delta_in_one_line: 0.30 mm is BELOW the published minimum of both houses at every layer count above two, and below JLCPCB's overall minimum at any layer count. PCBWay lists 0.2 mm for 1-2 layer, so a 2-layer 0.30 mm is inside their envelope while 0.30 mm is not one of their listed thickness options.
fabricator_capability._what_this_does_NOT_tell_us: NOTHING about Apple. These are prototype houses. Apple's board suppliers build any-layer HDI at volumes and tolerances no prototype capability page describes. A capability page bounds what WE can order; it does not bound what Apple built. Fusing those two is the error this file exists to prevent.

core_stock_series.source: allpcb, 'Standard FR-4 cores come in thicknesses like 0.1mm, 0.2mm, 0.3mm, 0.4mm, 0.5mm, 0.7mm, 1.0mm, and 1.5mm' — https://www.allpcb.com/allelectrohub/the-definitive-guide-to-pcb-core-thickness-choosing-whats-right-for-your-design , fetched 2026-09-05
core_stock_series._caveat: One vendor's stocked series. A different house stocks a different series, and a fab-quoted stackup beats this list. Used to answer 'is this dielectric height made of a material that exists', not to specify a build.
